name: dmesg
description: Prints the kernel ring buffer: boot messages, hardware detection, driver errors, and runtime kernel events.

flags.description: Human-readable timestamps instead of seconds since boot.

examples.explanation: The last 20 kernel events with real timestamps — the first check when hardware acts up.

examples.output:
[Tue Jan 12 09:41:02 2025] usb 1-2: new high-speed USB device
[Tue Jan 12 09:41:03 2025] sd 6:0:0:0: [sdb] Attached SCSI removable disk
examples.explanation: Filters for problems and USB events — here a USB stick was just plugged in and became sdb.
Only warnings and errors, cleanly separated from informational noise.

about: The ring buffer holds the kernel's own messages, including everything from boot (before syslog starts). With systemd, the same content is available via journalctl -k with better filtering and persistence. dmesg shows OOM kills, disk errors, USB events, and driver problems that never reach application logs.
mistakes: Reading raw second-based timestamps and misjudging when things happened — use -T.
Looking for application errors in dmesg — those live in the journal/app logs.
warnings: On some hardened systems, unprivileged dmesg is restricted (kernel.dmesg_restrict=1); use sudo.
